messages.text: [P4-6 · S] ⟨contingent: PRE-B, PRE-D⟩ Release readiness: README, install docs, license scan of the dependency tree, final name. CONTINGENT ON PRE-B (has anyone asked for this) and PRE-D (rename — 'Token Tracker' is an established OSS project).

[P4-5 · S] Collector conformance harness — non-blocking, informational. Replays fixtures/claude-session-scrubbed.jsonl against a candidate collector and reports whether it dedups (2.41x inflation if not) and buckets cache correctly (cache read is 97.4% of tokens). AC: produces a report; never gates the build.

[P4-4 · M] `lum doctor`: which sources were looked for and found, snapshot age, which signal is primary and why, config aliases in effect, and what to install if nothing is present. AC: fits 80 columns; names a concrete next action in every degraded state.

[P4-3 · S] ⟨contingent: PRE-A⟩ Source selection: config `source: auto|budi|ccusage|tokentracker`, probing in a deterministic order. AC: with several collectors present the choice is deterministic and explained by `lum doctor`.
[P4-2 · M] ⟨contingent: PRE-A⟩ tokentracker.ts — third adapter, 34-tool coverage. AC: passes the P1-3 contract suite unmodified.

[P4-1 · M] ⟨contingent: PRE-A, PRE-E⟩ ccusage.shellout.ts — the ZERO-INSTALL path for Claude+Codex-only users, and the main mitigation for R1 (doubled install friction). AC: passes the P1-3 contract suite unmodified; works with no daemon running at all.

[P3-6 · S] ⟨contingent: PRE-F⟩ Snapshot refresh trigger. CONTINGENT ON PRE-F — builds the CONSENTED path only (explicit `lum refresh`, cron/launchd documented). The zero-config alternative is a detached spawn, which is the unanswered consent question. DO NOT implement a self-spawn without a human decision on PRE-F.
[P3-5 · S] `lum install-statusline` — patch ~/.claude/settings.json with a backup. AC: idempotent; refuses to clobber an existing unrelated statusLine without an explicit flag.

[P3-4 · M] Latency budget asserted in CI as three layers, because absolute spawn p95 on a shared runner is unassertable. AC: the three layers are defined, measured and enforced; the in-process render path is well under budget.

[P3-3 · S] render/statusline.ts per DESIGN §5-§7: rate-limit-primary variants, 'worst window wins' (max(5h%,7d%) drives the shared bar and latch state), pacing glyph, the five degradation states. AC: 16-colour fallback verified under TERM=xterm; NO_COLOR honoured; colour is never the only signal.

[P3-2 · M] stdin parsing plus the rate-limit echo file (~200 bytes). rate_limits arrives ONLY on the statusline's stdin, so without this echo the signal ADR-v2-003 makes primary reaches one surface out of three. AC: rate_limits absent, one window absent, and both present all handled; absence degrades to USD silently and never errors.

[P3-1 · M] bin/statusline.js — thin reader, node:fs only, ALWAYS exit 0, consumes and discards stdin so it can never block on the pipe. AC: exit 0 under every injected fault (missing, corrupt, stale, empty snapshot).

[P2-5 · S] Wire budget + pacing + latch into the meter. AC: crossing 0.8 then 1.0 fires exactly one notification each; restarting the process re-fires nothing; a dip below and back up re-fires nothing.
[P2-4 · S] Notifier: osascript / notify-send / PowerShell / bell fallback, user-overridable command. AC: fires once per threshold per usage-day; text contains no path, project name or prompt content.

[P2-3 · M] The threshold latch — the correctness centrepiece. Pure evaluateLatch() with nine rules: replace-not-merge on day change, dips never clear, corrupt state fails quiet, persist-then-notify, and L9 never fire from untrusted data. AC: six named tests including a fast-check property and a genuine two-process restart test.

[P2-2 · S] domain/pacing.ts: expected-vs-actual for elapsed fraction of the usage day. AC: suppressed below 15% elapsed and inside the 5pp deadzone (both DESIGN defaults are unmeasured and flagged as such); never rendered in a threshold colour.

[P2-1 · S] ⟨contingent: OPEN-F⟩ domain/budget.ts: evaluate(spend, cfg) -> {fraction, state, crossed[]}. AC: pure, table-driven tests over the threshold boundaries. CONTINGENT ON OPEN-F — currently scoped to the USD fraction only; if thresholds are ruled to follow the primary signal, this takes the signal as a parameter.

[P1-9 · S] Structural gates: no content field ever reaches a record; no network primitive outside the loopback adapter; canary-string test. Lands in P1 and stays green forever. AC: all three assertions run in CI and fail the build when violated.

[P1-8 · M] `lum today` plus the nine-row degradation matrix, and config loading with clis→tools and imputeCostForSubscription→primarySignal accepted as aliases. AC: every row of the matrix renders its stated output; UNKNOWN NEVER RENDERS AS $0.00.
[P1-7 · M] app/meter.ts: pull source, build snapshot. AC: per-tool figures sum exactly to the total; a partial collector response is marked partial, never silently completed.
[P1-6 · S] Atomic store: tmp + fsync + rename for the latch and cache. AC: kill -9 mid-write leaves a valid previous file; readers never observe a torn file.

[P1-5 · S] Second real adapter, pulled forward from P4 deliberately. AC: passes the same P1-3 suite unmodified. From this point two real implementations prove the port is a real seam and not decoration.

[P1-4 · M] Primary source adapter (budi.http.ts, or whichever P0-4's verdict selected). All collector contact confined to this one file. AC: passes the P1-3 suite unmodified; a daemon-down response degrades rather than throwing.

[P1-3 · M] The 14-case UsageSourcePort contract suite plus an in-memory reference adapter replaying P0-5 fixtures. DO THIS BEFORE THE FIRST REAL ADAPTER — it is the mitigation for R2 and it only works if it exists first. AC: suite green against the reference adapter; every adapter added later runs the identical suite unmodified.
[P1-2 · S] usageDayFor(ts, resetHourLocal, tz) plus window bounds. AC: DST transition days, a non-zero resetHour, and a clock jump across the boundary all covered by tests.

[P1-1 · S] Domain types and ports: ToolSpend, UsageWindow, UsageSnapshot, Config, Threshold, and the port interfaces. Pure — no fs, no net, no clock. AC: domain/ compiles with zero imports outside itself.
[P1-0 · M] Scaffold: package.json (ESM, Node >=20.11), tsconfig strict, vitest, biome, CI skeleton. AC: `npm test` and lint run green on an empty suite.
[P0-5 · S] Freeze the recorded responses as contract fixtures for the P1 suite. AC: fixtures committed; the in-memory reference adapter in P1-3 can replay them offline with no collector installed.

[P0-4 · S] Apply the 8-row decision rule and write SPIKE_RESULT.md. AC: exactly one verdict recorded (GO / GO-fallback / GO-reorder / CONDITIONAL / PARTIAL / INCONCLUSIVE / NO-GO) with the observations that produced it. DO NOT mark PRE-C resolved — report the finding and let the human close the gate. This board's predecessor lost a gate to an agent that closed its own escalation.

[P0-3 · S] Probe the CLI paths — `budi stats --format json` AND `ccusage daily --json --offline` — in the same sitting. The §7 fallback assumed the CLI is day-shaped; RESEARCH only established it is MORE STABLE, a different property. AC: both CLI shapes recorded against D1-D4, so the fallback is evidence-based rather than assumed.

[P0-2 · S] Probe GET /analytics/*. Capture raw responses verbatim. Test the four day-shaped criteria: D1 a window/day dimension, D2 collector-computed USD, D3 a per-tool dimension, D4 idempotent totals for a past day. AC: raw JSON saved; each of D1-D4 marked pass/fail with the evidence.

[P0-1 · S] Environment and route discovery. Confirm which collectors exist on the machine and enumerate the daemon's real routes (e.g. `strings $(command -v budi)`) BEFORE guessing URLs with curl. Record versions. AC: a written list of reachable routes, or an explicit 'no collector installed' finding.

p4-portability-doctor: Make no collector load-bearing. A third adapter, source selection, `lum doctor`, a collector conformance harness, and release readiness. Runs PARALLEL to p2/p3 — it depends only on the port from p1, not on the budget layer. This goal is what turns R2 from a risk into an inconvenience.

p3-statusline-surface: The primary surface. A thin always-exit-0 statusline reading only node:fs, stdin parsing for rate_limits (the binding constraint on subscription accounts), the rate-limit echo file so `lum today` and `lum doctor` can see a signal that otherwise only reaches one surface of three, rendering, and a latency budget asserted in CI as three layers rather than an unassertable absolute p95. Contains the PRE-F contingent task.

p2-budget-pacing-latch: THE WEDGE — the part no competitor has. Budget evaluation, pacing (spend vs elapsed usage-day), the threshold latch, and the notifier. The latch is the correctness centrepiece: exactly once per threshold per usage-day, surviving process restart, never re-arming on a dip below, and — rule L9 — never firing from stale, partial or source-down data. An alert derived from a number we are not sure of is worse than no alert: it teaches the user to ignore alerts.

p1-core-port-today: The spine. Pure domain types, UsageSourcePort, the 14-case contract suite, TWO real adapters, atomic store, the meter pull, `lum today` with its nine-row degradation matrix, and the structural privacy/import/network gates. The contract suite lands BEFORE the first real adapter and the second adapter is pulled forward from P4 on purpose: two implementations must exercise the port from P1 onward, otherwise Risk R2 (budi is a solo project, 0 external PRs) sits unmitigated for three phases and the port is decoration.

p0-collector-spike: Prove the collector API can answer 'what did each tool cost today'. GO/NO-GO GATE for the entire board — nothing downstream is worth building until this returns real, day-shaped, per-tool numbers. Defines 'day-shaped' as four testable criteria and applies an 8-row decision table covering GO / GO-fallback / GO-reorder / CONDITIONAL / PARTIAL / INCONCLUSIVE / NO-GO. 'No collector on the spike machine' is INCONCLUSIVE, not a failure. Closes PRE-C. Freezes recorded responses as contract fixtures for P1.

WE NEVER COLLECT USAGE. Every number enters through UsageSourcePort from a collector already installed on the machine. No JSONL parsing, no tail, no dedup, no pricing table, no reconciler, no daemon of our own — those all exist in the archived v1 design and are deleted. Anyone proposing to build them has misread the plan. Corollary: the collector's HTTP API is a local daemon's INTERNAL surface, not a published contract; all contact stays inside one adapter file behind the port.

[OPEN-F] Do thresholds apply to the primary signal or to USD? ADR-v2-003 makes rate-limit % the subscription headline, but thresholds evaluate the USD fraction — so the default user is warned when imputed dollars (money that does not exist) cross a budget she invented. The product's entire wedge is the warning, and it currently fires on the wrong number.

[PRE-F] Who writes the statusline's cache? The statusline can only read (node:fs only) and lum does not reside in memory, so nothing refreshes the meter unless the user types lum — the zero-config promise is broken at the root. The only zero-config fix is a detached spawn, which is the consent question this board's predecessor never answered and wrongly recorded as 'resolved by deletion'. Options A/B/C in ARCHITECTURE §6. Planning ASSUMES B (opt-in).
[PRE-E] Is doubled install friction acceptable? Users must install a 13 MB Rust collector before this tool does anything. The brief promised 'setup is trivial'. Main adoption threat (R1).
[PRE-D] Rename. 'Token Tracker' is an established OSS project doing exactly this, and the repo is currently named token-tracker. Cheapest to fix now.

[PRE-C] Does budi GET /analytics/* return day-shaped per-tool spend? One curl. This is the P0 go/no-go gate for the entire board. Task P0-4 explicitly instructs the builder NOT to close this gate themselves.

[PRE-B] Has anyone actually asked for this? No budget/alert issue has ever been filed on budi. Unclaimed and unwanted look identical from outside. File the issue before building — cheapest possible validation.

[PRE-A] Exact tool list. The brief says Claude Code + Codex; the stated market also uses Cursor and more. Decides collector choice and adapter scope. Planning ASSUMES {Claude Code, Codex, Cursor} — that is an assumption, not a decision.

IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — 30 tasks across P0-P4 with ids, goals, files, deps, acceptance criteria and S/M/L sizes. P0 is a real gate: 'day-shaped' is four testable criteria plus an 8-row decision table covering GO / fallback / conditional / inconclusive / no-go. The 14-case UsageSourcePort contract suite lands at P1-3 and a second adapter at P1-5, so two real implementations exercise it from P1 onward. Latch spec has nine rules including L9: never fire from untrusted data.

USER_STORIES — 12 Given/When/Then stories for a multi-tool developer, MoSCoW-prioritised, each with testable acceptance criteria and a phase mapping. Stories contingent on an open gate carry an explicit ASSUMES marker. Two of the original brief's acceptance tests are untestable by us under ADR-v2-001 and are recorded as collector-selection criteria instead.

DESIGN — palette, ANSI codes with 16-colour fallback, threshold colours, notification copy, accessibility. Sections 5-8 are the v2 surfaces: the rate-limit-primary statusline (one/both/neither window present; 'worst window wins' — max(5h%, 7d%) drives the shared bar and the latch), the pacing glyph and its suppression rules, the five-state degradation taxonomy, and the lum today per-tool table. Two rules there are correctness not cosmetics: unknown must never render as $0.00, and notifications fire only from fresh data.

ARCHITECTURE v2 — consume a collector, own the budget policy. Three decisions carry it: never parse a log; no daemon of our own; read the statusline's stdin (rate_limits is the binding constraint on subscriptions). Layers, the UsageSourcePort contract, config, four ADRs, six risks. Contains two UNRESOLVED defects found by review and left open: PRE-F (the statusline cache has no writer, so the zero-config promise is broken) and OPEN-F (thresholds fire on USD while the subscription headline is rate-limit %). v1 is archived under archive/ and must not be treated as current.

PO_NOTES — personas, success criteria, constraints, out-of-scope. Primary persona is a multi-tool developer who is NOT the author: uses Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more in one day, each with its own console and limit, and wants one allowance across all of them. Note the author's own machine measured 100.0% Claude Code / 0.001% Codex over 30 days and is not representative.

SPEC — the build contract for this board. What we build (a budget guardrail), what we explicitly do not (any usage collection), the UsageSourcePort integration contract, scope in/out, size (30 tasks: 18 S, 12 M, zero L; ~1,400 LOC production), the five phases, seven OPEN human decisions, five risks, and the definition of done. Read this first.

Goal: LocalUsageMeter budget layer — a local budget guardrail that reads today spend from an already-installed usage collector (budi / ccusage / Token Tracker) over loopback, compares it to a configurable allowance across every AI coding tool the developer uses, and warns before the allowance is gone. We govern usage, we never collect it. The collection layer is commoditised; the budget-and-alert layer is unclaimed.
